dedupe_keys.name: uavnoma two user uav communications model

description: uavnoma implements a downlink communications model with one unmanned aerial vehicle and two ground users. Brena Lima and collaborators publish Python functions and a command-line interface for positions, channel gains, interference and performance calculations. The model includes imperfect successive interference cancellation and residual hardware impairments. Its spatial coverage and parameter ranges are user-defined, not a fixed geographic network or monitoring period. Achievable-rate and outage-probability outputs can support capacity studies for aerial telecommunications links and exploration of power allocation. Source access is free under MIT, with NumPy, pandas and plotting dependencies documented. A limitation is the deliberately small two-user topology and its specific channel assumptions; larger cooperative or full-duplex networks require extensions. It complements broader communications-network simulations through a reusable link-level model. The code and usage documentation were inspected without installation, Monte Carlo runs or independent verification of numerical results.
